title: Naming a Company
summary: Given an array of strings representing potential company names, select two distinct names, swap their first letters, and check if the modified names are not in the original list.
statement: Given an array of strings representing potential company names, select two distinct names, swap their first letters, and check if the modified names are not in the original list. Count the number of valid names formed by concatenating the modified names.
constraints: Choose two distinct original ideas in order and swap their first letters.
A company name is valid only when both newly formed words are absent from the original idea set.
Count ordered company names, so reversing the two resulting words is a different name.
hints: Group suffixes by their original first letter.
For two initial groups, suffixes present in both cannot participate because one swapped word would already exist.
Multiply the exclusive suffix counts and multiply by two for the two ordered company names.
Every valid swap chooses one exclusive suffix from each group, and every such choice creates two absent words, establishing a bijection.
editorial: Every valid swap chooses one exclusive suffix from each group, and every such choice creates two absent words, establishing a bijection.

tests.explanation: Valid swaps between the c/d suffix groups and t/d groups produce six ordered names.
Swapping initials recreates the two original ideas, so no valid name exists.
